methodology.timing: Node performance.now surrounds one exported MoonBit operation; no JSON or report serialization inside timing.
methodology.session: One opaque fixture with one persistent Session per isolated worker; repeated previews and updates reuse that cache. Valid updates alternate old/new values.
methodology.optimizations: Round 1 hashes removals/additions, derives actual changes from supplied deltas and existing graph indexes, and indexes changed Objects/Subjects/Outgoing reads. Preview does not populate a next cache: reused results are still deep-copied, while newly evaluated isolated results are returned directly. Round 2 retains already-unique old triples, visits additions in input order using a first-representative flag and original SPO membership, and calls an internal Graph::from_unique constructor to rebuild SPO/POS indexes without another full-triple deduplication map. Public Graph::new still deduplicates arbitrary input. Reader dependency collection, cache invalidation, target enumeration, and semantic validation remain active, with no full-validation fallback. All candidate construction, changes, dependency checks, and index reconstruction remain timed. All-people has zero reused validation results, so its gain is not semantic-cache reuse alone.
methodology.cold: Fresh parsing and compilation rebuild objects each call; VM/JIT is warmed. OS file I/O, process start, module import and data generation are excluded.
methodology.fairness: Full validation on a prebuilt candidate excludes graph construction. The original rebuildAndValidateInvalidFull comparator is retained unchanged: linear removals.contains filtering, public Graph API construction, and full validation. The primary comparator rebuildAndValidateInvalidFullHashed was introduced in round 1 and is unchanged in round 2: it replaces only the removal lookup with a fresh Map<Triple,Bool>, charging its construction inside the timing. Both full comparators use the same public Graph API and defensive triples() copy, reconstruct all indexes and run full validation. The session uses internal ownership/uniqueness knowledge to omit redundant full-triple deduplication; it still rebuilds indexes and tracks changes and dependencies. Ratios therefore compare complete implementation paths, not isolated semantic-cache benefit. Before/after checks require both candidate triple sequences and full recursive reports to match.
methodology.memory: Bytes from process.memoryUsage snapshots. baseline/fixture/final snapshots follow explicit GC; operation snapshots bracket whole sample batches. No intra-operation peak or allocation-rate measurement. Fixture includes Turtle strings, two graphs, shapes, plan, session/cache and deltas; its delta is not cache-only overhead.
methodology.gc: Explicit GC before sample batches, never inside timed calls; naturally occurring GC remains in sample durations.
methodology.scope: Synthetic Person/company sequence-path workload, not a production dataset, cross-engine ranking or general throughput claim.

historicalComparison.limitation: The original pre-optimization archive and current run are separate runs, not randomized paired measurements. Comparison is cache-preview latency against its own prior implementation; the hashed full baseline was introduced in round 1, did not exist in this original archive, and must not be substituted into its old ratios.

previousRoundComparison.limitation: The previous-round archive and current run are separate runs, not randomized or interleaved paired measurements. Both already include the same hashed full comparator. Preview self-speedup and the within-run full/preview ratio answer different questions. All-people reuses zero validation results; candidate-construction savings must not be described as semantic-cache reuse.
